content.title: Class-Weighted Evaluation Metrics for Imbalanced Data Classification
content.abstract: Class distribution skews in imbalanced datasets may lead to models with prediction bias towards majority classes, making fair assessment of classifiers a challenging task. Metrics such as Balanced Accuracy are commonly used to evaluate a classifier’s prediction performance under such scenarios. However, these metrics fall short when classes vary in importance. In this paper, we propose a simple and general-purpose evaluation framework for imbalanced data classification that is sensitive to arbitrary skews in class cardinalities and importances. Experiments with several state-of-the-art classifiers tested on real-world datasets from three different domains show the effectiveness of our framework – not only in evaluating and ranking classifiers, but also training them.
content.one-sentence_summary: This paper presents a new evaluation framework for imbalanced data classification that can be used to train, evaluate, and rank models in a way that is sensitive to arbitrary skews in class cardinalities and importances.
